sentences.en: I'm Gemma Spake, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through the biggest changes, moments, and transitions of our 20s,
sentences.zh: 我是杰玛·斯派克，欢迎回到《你二十岁的心理学》，这是一档探讨我们二十岁时经历的最大变化、时刻与转变，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们的心理意味着什么的播客。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能来收听又一期节目，当然，我们要在这里剖析二十岁的心理学。

sentences.en: Today, we are talking about time, specifically why it seems to move so much faster as we get older and why the months just seem to be shorter and shorter every single year.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来聊聊时间，具体来说，为什么随着我们变老，时间似乎过得越来越快，为什么每个月似乎都在一年比一年变短。

sentences.en: I want you to think back for a second to being a kid and to being a kid in summer.
sentences.zh: 我想让你回想一下自己还是个孩子的时候，回想一下夏天的童年时光。

sentences.en: Like, those summers used to feel absolutely endless.
sentences.zh: 比如，那些夏天过去感觉简直无边无际。

sentences.en: You'd go back to school and it felt like a lifetime had passed.
sentences.zh: 等你重返学校时，感觉仿佛已经过去了一辈子。

sentences.en: Three months felt like eternity.
sentences.zh: 三个月感觉就像永恒。

sentences.en: Every six months, you felt like you were a new person.
sentences.zh: 每隔六个月，你都会觉得自己变成了一个崭新的人。

sentences.en: Compare that to now, where an entire year can go by and you will swear it's been a couple of weeks.
sentences.zh: 跟现在对比一下，现在一整年都可以过去，而你发誓感觉才过了几个星期。

sentences.en: Where did that endless feeling kind of go?
sentences.zh: 那种无边无际的感觉到底去哪了？

sentences.en: Where did it disappear to?
sentences.zh: 它消失到哪里去了？

sentences.en: I think a lot of us can point to a very specific moment where our relationship with time kind of broke, and that's probably during COVID.
sentences.zh: 我想我们很多人都能指出一个非常具体的时刻，当时我们与时间的关系某种程度上破裂了，那很可能是在疫情期间。

sentences.en: Suddenly, our days had no shape.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，我们的日子失去了形状。

sentences.en: There was no commute, no plans, no real distinction between a Tuesday and a Saturday.
sentences.zh: 没有通勤，没有计划，星期二和星期六之间没有真正的区别。

sentences.en: And for a lot of us, especially anyone who was a teenager or in their early 20s at the time,
sentences.zh: 对于我们中的许多人，尤其是当时正处于青少年时期或二十岁出头的人来说，

sentences.en: I think months just kind of dissolved into each other.
sentences.zh: 我觉得月份就这样彼此融化交织在了一起。

sentences.en: And I don't think many of us have fully gotten that sense of structured, meaningful time back.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得我们中没有几个人完全找回那种结构化、有意义的时间感。

sentences.en: The days just get faster and faster.
sentences.zh: 日子只是变得越来越快。

sentences.en: So today, we are going to actually unpack this.
sentences.zh: 所以今天，我们要真正来剖析这个现象。

sentences.en: Why does time feel like it speeds up as we get older?
sentences.zh: 为什么随着年龄的增长，时间会感觉在加速？

sentences.en: And how do we slow it right back down again using actual psychology and actual science?
sentences.zh: 我们又该如何利用真正的心理学和真正的科学，把时间硬生生地慢下来呢？

sentences.en: So we're going to talk about the different types of time, the ways that time can be measured, especially how they are understood across cultures,
sentences.zh: 所以我们要聊聊不同类型的时间、衡量时间的方式，特别是它们在不同文化中是如何被理解的，

sentences.en: how memory and novelty play into all of this, how being online, our digital lives have changed our perception of time.
sentences.zh: 记忆和新鲜感是如何融入这一切的，以及我们的数字生活——上网如何改变了我们对时间的感知。

sentences.en: And then, most importantly, as promised, the three things that will make your life and your days and your years feel longer without you having to do very much at all.
sentences.zh: 然后，最重要的是，正如承诺的那样，这三个方法能让你的生活、日子和年份感觉更长，而你甚至不需要做太多事情。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 废话不多说，我们切入正题吧。

sentences.en: So in order to really start answering questions about time passing us by with age and why that feels faster, we do need to understand how time is even measured in the first place.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了真正开始解答关于时间随着年龄流逝以及为什么感觉变快的问题，我们确实需要先了解时间最初是如何被度量的。

sentences.en: And I know it feels silly and quite obvious to ask things like, you know, what is time?
sentences.zh: 我知道问诸如“什么是时间”之类的问题听起来很傻，也很显而易见。

sentences.en: It's very like philosophical because I feel like we all kind of know it's something ingrained in us very deeply, but there are levels to this.
sentences.zh: 这非常像哲学问题，因为我觉得我们都觉得时间是某种深深植根于我们内心的东西，但这是有层次的。

sentences.en: There's always levels to things like this.
sentences.zh: 这种事情总是分层次的。

sentences.en: Your sense of time originates in the brain.
sentences.zh: 你对时间的感知源于大脑。

sentences.en: Different regions keep track of different aspects of your environment that anchor your time perception.
sentences.zh: 不同的区域负责追踪你环境中锚定时间感知的不同方面。

sentences.en: For example, things like daylight, things like exhaustion, things like movement, attention.
sentences.zh: 例如，日光、疲劳、运动、注意力等事物。

sentences.en: Interestingly, the evidence suggests that there may be a separate clock for each of our senses and that they all kind of talk and coordinate and communicate
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，证据表明，我们的每一个感官可能都有一个独立的时钟，它们会相互交谈、协调和沟通，

sentences.en: to just give us a sense of where we are in a day, where we are in a moment, where we are in our lives.
sentences.zh: 从而让我们对自己在一天中的位置、在某一时刻的位置、在生活中的位置有一个整体的感知。

sentences.en: Based on what you are experiencing, time can either dilate and feel like it's passing slower, like when you're bored, or it can contract and feel like it's speeding up,
sentences.zh: 根据你的经历，时间要么会膨胀并感觉过得更慢，比如当你感到无聊时；要么会收缩并感觉在加速，

sentences.en: like when you're in a flow state or when you're in a really good conversation or you're drunk and you're partying and suddenly it's 2 a.m.
sentences.zh: 比如当你进入心流状态，或者正在进行一场非常愉快的对话，或者你喝醉了在派对狂欢，突然就凌晨两点了。

sentences.en: All of this is based in your brain.
sentences.zh: 这一切都植根于你的大脑。

sentences.en: So the neurological experience of time is one thing.
sentences.zh: 所以对时间的神经学体验是一回事。

sentences.en: Then there is the social experience or social measurement of time, which is a lot more critical for what we're talking about today.
sentences.zh: 然后是对时间的社会体验或社会度量，这对于我们今天讨论的主题要关键得多。

sentences.en: Things like morning, like noon, like bedtime, 2 p.m., lunchtime, midnight, that is what we would call the standard measurement of time or the social measurement of time.
sentences.zh: 比如早晨、正午、睡前、下午两点、午餐时间、午夜，这就是我们所说的标准时间度量或社会时间度量。

sentences.en: However, the typical units of measurement that we use, so minutes, seconds, weeks, years, that kind of stuff, they're just made up.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们所使用的典型度量单位，比如分钟、秒、周、年之类的东西，其实都是虚构出来的。

sentences.en: They're made up.
sentences.zh: 它们是编造的。

sentences.en: We just use them to communicate and get on the same page.
sentences.zh: 我们只是用它们来沟通并达成共识。

sentences.en: At some point, someone decided
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，有人决定

sentences.en: 60 seconds made a minute.
sentences.zh: 60秒等于一分钟。

sentences.en: 60 minutes made an hour, simply because it was very easy to divide.
sentences.zh: 60分钟等于一小时，仅仅是因为这样非常容易除尽。

sentences.en: That's like the one theory.
sentences.zh: 这就是其中一种理论。

sentences.en: It was an easily divisible number.
sentences.zh: 它是一个很容易除尽的数字。

sentences.en: That's why it was chosen.
sentences.zh: 这就是它被选中的原因。

sentences.en: Measured time is therefore what we call a social construct.
sentences.zh: 因此，被度量的时间是我们所说的社会建构。

sentences.en: And how time feels to us beyond that, psychologically, is also very cultural.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，时间在心理上对我们的感觉如何，也带有很强的文化色彩。

sentences.en: So historically, and now we're really getting into the history here, but time has been measured differently by different cultures.
sentences.zh: 所以从历史上看——现在我们真的要深入探讨历史了——不同文化对时间的度量方式是不同的。

sentences.en: Kind of makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这其实挺好理解的。

sentences.en: But agricultural societies used to measure time by changing seasons and crop rotations.
sentences.zh: 但农业社会曾经通过季节更替和农作物轮作来度量时间。

sentences.en: Others went by like the position of the sun moon and the moon.
sentences.zh: 其他人则根据太阳和月亮的位置来判断。

sentences.en: That's what led to the invention of the sundial, the first like original kind of clock, measurement of time.
sentences.zh: 这就催生了日淠的发明，这是最早的、最初的那种时钟和时间度量工具。

sentences.en: Interestingly, there is an anthropologist, his name is Edward T.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，有一位人类学家，他的名字叫爱德华·T·

sentences.en: Hall.
sentences.zh: 霍尔。

sentences.en: And he argued that Western societies, we see time as fixed and perpetual, which is why we like to think about things sequentially and chronologically.
sentences.zh: 他认为，在西方社会，我们将时间视为固定且永恒的，这就是为什么我们喜欢按顺序和按年代来思考事物。

sentences.en: And we really like ideas of progress and we like ideas of growth.
sentences.zh: 我们非常喜欢进步的观念，也喜欢成长的观念。

sentences.en: And our behaviors and timelines
sentences.zh: 我们的行为和时间表

sentences.en: are shaped by this experience and how we see time as kind of this segmented thing that moves forward.
sentences.zh: 正是由这种体验以及我们将时间视为一种向前推进的片段化事物的视角所塑造的。

sentences.en: On the other hand, he and his kind of research and travels saw how other societies, like those in Latin America and those in Asia, are what we call polychronic,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，通过他的研究和旅行，他看到其他社会，比如拉丁美洲和亚洲的社会，属于我们所说的多向时间观（多任务时间观），

sentences.en: meaning time is viewed more as a stream that ebbs and flows.
sentences.zh: 这意味着时间被更多地视为一条起伏流淌的溪流。

sentences.en: A lot can happen all at once and then they can be nothing for years.
sentences.zh: 很多事情可以同时发生，然后可能好几年什么都没有。

sentences.en: Nothing for years.
sentences.zh: 好几年什么都没有。

sentences.en: I also came across this writing by the Kenyan-born philosopher,
sentences.zh: 我还偶然读到了一位出生于肯尼亚的哲学家撰写的文章，

sentences.en: John Minbiti, and he notes how
sentences.zh: 他叫约翰·姆比蒂，他指出

sentences.en: Kenyan belief specifically doesn't conceptualize the future at all.
sentences.zh: 肯尼亚人的信仰具体根本没有对未来的概念。

sentences.en: Because in his view, time needs to be, well, not in his view, in their view, time needs to be experienced in order to be real.
sentences.zh: 因为在他看来，时间需要——好吧，不是在他看来，在他们的看来，时间必须被体验才能成为现实。

sentences.en: So future time is not a concept.
sentences.zh: 所以未来时间并不是一个概念。

sentences.en: Since it's impossible to experience the future, like, it just doesn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 既然不可能体验未来，那么它就根本不存在。

sentences.en: Instead, like, you need, the future is only created by the present moment.
sentences.zh: 相反，未来仅仅是由当下这一刻创造出来的。

sentences.en: And you have to see how that perception that's passed along culturally will influence how people view the future and how people view planning and how people view death
sentences.zh: 你必须明白，这种通过文化传承下来的感知将如何影响人们对未来的看法、对规划的看法、对死亡的看法

sentences.en: and all these sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 以及所有这类事情。

sentences.en: So as we've evolved, we've definitely tried to get more specific and unified across different locations and different cultures.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着我们的进化，我们绝对试图在不同的地点和不同的文化中变得更加具体和统一。

sentences.en: especially for capitalism, especially for the purpose of trade.
sentences.zh: 特别是为了资本主义，特别是为了贸易的目的。

sentences.en: And that is why we kind of invented standard time zones.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们发明了标准时区。

sentences.en: And that's why we invented a coordinated universal time where we kind of all, we can kind of know what time it is in Sydney versus what time in London versus Kenya.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么我们发明了协调世界时，让我们所有人都能大致了解悉尼是什么时间，伦敦是什么时间，肯尼亚又是什么时间。

sentences.en: Despite that, each of us will still experience time differently.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，我们每个人对时间的体验仍然会有所不同。

sentences.en: Our perception of time is very unique.
sentences.zh: 我们对时间的感知是非常独特的。

sentences.en: It varies from person to person, regardless of what the time on a clock or on your phone says.
sentences.zh: 它因人而异，无论时钟或手机上的时间显示的是什么。

sentences.en: 10 minutes to me might not feel the same as it does to you or the next person, even if it's measured the same way.
sentences.zh: 对我来说的10分钟，感觉可能和你或其他人感受到的不同，即使它的度量方式完全相同。

sentences.en: It depends on what we have going on.
sentences.zh: 这取决于我们正在忙些什么。

sentences.en: It depends on how we mark time personally.
sentences.zh: 这取决于我们如何个人化地标记时间。

sentences.en: For example, do you mark time by big moments or novel moments or sleep or productivity or days?
sentences.zh: 例如，你是用重大时刻、新鲜时刻、睡眠、生产力还是日子来标记时间？

sentences.en: It changes if we're listening to music.
sentences.zh: 如果我们正在听音乐，感觉就会变。

sentences.en: It changes if we're in a flow state.
sentences.zh: 如果我们处于心流状态，感觉也会变。

sentences.en: And it just changes because of other overarching personality factors like patience levels, temperament, even how you were raised.
sentences.zh: 它还会因为其他总体人格因素而改变，比如耐心水平、气质，甚至是你的成长背景。

sentences.en: And this is the third face of time.
sentences.zh: 这就是时间的第三个面相。

sentences.en: The one that stems from your own psychology and your own experiences.
sentences.zh: 这个面相源于你自己的心理和你的亲身经历。

sentences.en: And the one that we really need to explore to kind of understand why time feels so much faster now than it did when we were little kids or than it did when we were in COVID.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们需要去探索的面相，以便理解为什么现在的时间感觉比我们小时候或疫情期间要快得多。

sentences.en: One thing that we know really influences our perception of time more than anything else is novelty.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，有一件事对我们时间感知的巨大影响超过其他任何事物，那就是新鲜感。

sentences.en: Basically, novelty is the more new things you experience, the more newness you have in your life.
sentences.zh: 基本上，新鲜感就是你体验的新事物越多，你生活中的新奇事物就越多。

sentences.en: The more of that, the more that those long stretches of time are broken up by things that kind of create distinct snapshots.
sentences.zh: 这种东西越多，那些漫长的时间段就被那些创造出清晰快照的事物切割得越碎。

sentences.en: I know I said that time seems to speed up when we're really interested in something or when we're having a lot of fun or we're curious or we're excited but those moments
sentences.zh: 我知道我曾说过，当我们对某事真正感兴趣，或者玩得很开心、好奇、兴奋时，时间似乎会加速，但事后回想起来，

sentences.en: in hindsight seem to make time feel more expansive.
sentences.zh: 那些时刻会让时间感觉更加广阔。

sentences.en: So in the moment novelty speeds up time in hindsight it actually slows it down it makes it seem like you have more of it.
sentences.zh: 因此，在当下的新鲜感会加速时间，但在事后回想时，它实际上会放慢时间，让人觉得你拥有更多时间。

sentences.en: In a 2007 study published in the Journal of Vision researchers found that when people were exposed to two types of stimulus one which was exciting and large and colourful
sentences.zh: 在2007年发表在《视觉杂志》上的一项研究中，研究人员发现，当人们接触到两种类型的刺激——一种是令人兴奋、宏大、色彩缤纷且闪烁的，另一种是非常简单且略显无聊的——

sentences.en: and flashing and one which was very simple and slightly boring people thought that they saw the first stimulus the exciting one for longer despite seeing both the boring

sentences.zh: 记忆在这里至关重要。

sentences.zh: 为了创造一段记忆，大脑中的任何记忆，无论是谁的大脑，你的心智都需要先处理它确实发生了这件事。

sentences.en: Very simple, right?

sentences.zh: 但这对于记忆巩固至关重要。

sentences.zh: 当一段新鲜事件的时长被压缩到几秒甚至更短的空间里时，你知道的，也就是在TikTok上刷两三个视频所花费的时间，

sentences.en: What is worth consolidating?

sentences.en: The other thing that constant scrolling does is it makes it harder to consolidate memories that happen before and after you've been on your screen.

sentences.en: Now this specifically is a phenomenon called proactive interference.
sentences.zh: 现在，这具体是一种被称为前摄干扰的现象。

sentences.en: And it's when experiences outside of a memory interfere with that memory being processed.
sentences.zh: 当记忆之外的经历干扰了该记忆的处理时，就会发生这种情况。

sentences.en: I know that sounds a bit complicated but with the short form content specifically, your brain feels so overhyped and so stimulated so quickly.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来有点复杂，但特别是对于短视频内容，你的大脑会感觉过于亢奋，并在极短时间内受到过多刺激。

sentences.en: It is like we are so in on this, whatever just happened, we don't have time to solidify that.
